name: Sphingolipidosis

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient activity of specific lysosomal sphingolipid-degrading enzyme
Identification of pathogenic mutation(s) in genes encoding sphingolipid metabolism enzymes
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as organomegaly, neurological deterioration, and skeletal abnormalities
Histological evidence of sphingolipid accumulation in affected tissues
Elevated sphingolipid metabolites in blood or urine

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient enzyme activity or pathogenic genetic mutation plus characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of biochemical, genetic, and clinical data.

pathognomonic.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to lipid accumulation
Includes developmental delay, cognitive decline, and motor dysfunction
Characteristic retinal finding in several sphingolipidoses

common.notes: Facial dysmorphism due to storage material

occasional.notes: Nerve dysfunction causing sensory and motor symptoms
Respiratory insufficiency due to lipid accumulation
Heart muscle disease in some subtypes

rare.notes: Accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in brain ventricles
Kidney dysfunction secondary to lipid storage

laboratory: Reduced activity of specific lysosomal sphingolipid-degrading enzymes (e.g., glucocerebrosidase, sphingomyelinase)
Elevated sphingolipid metabolites in plasma and urine
imaging: MRI showing brain atrophy and white matter changes
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes such as GBA, SMPD1, GALC, HEXA, and others depending on subtype
other: Histopathological identification of lipid-laden macrophages (foam cells) in tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic bone crises and marrow infiltration
Absence of cherry-red macula in most cases
Marked cherry-red macula with rapid neurodegeneration

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurodegeneration in infancy or early childhood
Presence of cherry-red macula on ophthalmologic exam
references: Brunetti-Pierri N, Scaglia F. Sphingolipidoses: Clinical features and diagnosis. In: GeneReviews. University of Washington; 2023.
Neufeld EF, Muenzer J. The mucopolysaccharidoses. In: The Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease. 8th ed. 2001.
